description: Five prompts probing whether the skill applies design principles or merely retrieves catalog entries. Prompt 1 is a recall baseline (catalog-match by name); prompts 2-5 are novel domains that should produce structurally-correct designs only if the universal principles transferred. The decisive overfit-detection test is comparing prompt 1's output to prompt 2's: if structurally identical with renamed shapes, principles transferred; if prompt 2 looks like the prompt-1 ticket-corpus design with s/TicketProxy/VulnReport/, the skill is template-matching rather than principle-applying.
iteration_strategy: Run prompts 1, 2, and 4 first (3-prompt tight battery). Iterate the skill if any fails. Add prompts 3 and 5 in iteration-2 if iteration-1 passes — those test layered co-fingerprints and edge-type-as-load-bearing variants which are higher-difficulty and worth getting clean baseline first.

evals.prompt:
The goal is to have a queryable form of project tickets across multiple source systems

to do so we should design a high performance substrate to ingest (1 way sync), store and define query strategy

we want to be able to perform a series of operations over the corpus

are there natural clusters of tickets?
are there duplicates?
what tickets are stale?
are there high entropy tasks that would unlock other tickets?
and so on
evals.expected_output: A WarmHub graph design hitting fingerprint #11 (External-Proxy Analysis Graph). Should produce TicketProxy as Thing with bodyExcerpt cap, Project as Thing for source identity, TicketClusterMembership as Pair-targeted assertion, DuplicateAssertion as Set-targeted (symmetric), BlocksAssertion as Pair-targeted (directional), content-addressed AnalyticalPolicy bound to expensive analytical assertions, anti-shapes section listing 'stale' as a query not a shape, and a question catalog tying each shape to specific Q IDs.
evals.purpose: Baseline recall test. Fingerprint #11 (External-Proxy Analysis Graph) is the natural match for a ticket corpus. This prompt SHOULD produce a clean design — failing here would mean the skill can't even retrieve, let alone apply.

assertions.text: Design uses `about: { set: [...] }` for the duplicate-of relationship (symmetric)
Design uses `about: { pair: [blocker, blocked] }` for the blocks relationship (directional)
TicketProxy is modeled as a Thing (entity with single canonical state), not as an assertion
Design includes a content-addressed AnalyticalPolicy (or equivalent named shape) with policyWref bindings on expensive analytical assertions
Design includes an anti-shapes / anti-queries section listing 'stale tickets', 'high-entropy', and 'needs triage' as derived queries, not durable shapes
Question catalog uses [R] / [M] / [F] status markers and 'earns pressure for' attribution per the query-catalog-template format
Design walks the convergence checkpoint explicitly (5 questions answered)
Design correctly identifies fingerprint #11 (External-Proxy Analysis Graph) by name or by structurally-equivalent description
Design does NOT use `originalWref: string` or any flat-string-wref-field pattern to encode a relationship endpoint (the duplicate-assertion v1 anti-pattern explicitly avoided)
Design caps ticket body bytes (e.g. bodyExcerpt with size limit) and points at the source system via sourceUrl rather than mirroring full body content

evals.prompt:
We're building a graph to track our software vulnerability lifecycle. Reports come in from multiple sources: internal pen-testing, external bug bounty submissions, automated SAST scanners, and CVE feeds. The same underlying vulnerability often gets reported multiple times by different reporters who describe it differently. Some vulnerabilities lead to security incidents; some incidents involve multiple co-exploited vulnerabilities. Some vulnerabilities are flagged but later determined to be false-positives or duplicates of known issues.

We want the graph to support:
- 'What's the full disclosure history of this vulnerability?'
- 'Find duplicate reports of the same underlying vulnerability across our sources.'
- 'Which vulnerabilities have been exploited in which incidents?'
- 'What's our triage queue — vulnerabilities reported recently with no determination yet?'
- 'Which vulnerabilities have the highest blast radius — most incidents traced back to them?'

Help us design this.
evals.expected_output: A WarmHub graph design that's structurally identical to the ticket-corpus design (prompt 1's expected output), with domain-specific names: VulnReport / Vuln / Incident as Thing proxies; SameVulnAssertion as Set-targeted; ExploitsInAssertion as Pair-targeted; content-addressed dedupe-policy shape; triage queue as derived query; blast-radius as derived query (count of ExploitsInAssertion grouped by vulnerability). The shape skeleton should mirror prompt 1's despite the entirely different vocabulary.
evals.purpose: THE OVERFIT DETECTOR. Same fingerprint as prompt 1 (#11) but vocabulary doesn't trigger catalog name-match (no ticket corpus, no duplicate clusters). If the skill produces a design with the same Pair/Set choices, content-addressed policy, anti-shapes section, and question catalog format — principles transferred. If it produces something noticeably worse, name-matching was doing more work than principle-application.

assertions.text: Design uses `about: { set: [...] }` for the same-underlying-vulnerability relationship (symmetric — A is same as B is same as A)
Design uses `about: { pair: [vulnerability, incident] }` (or analogous) for the exploited-in / caused-by relationship (directional)
Vulnerability reports / canonical vulnerabilities / incidents are modeled as external-proxy Things, not as assertions
Design includes content-addressed analytical-policy shape bound to dedupe-across-sources verdicts (expensive derivation justifies it per D3)
Design lists 'triage queue' and 'blast radius' as derived queries, not as durable shapes (no TriageItem/BlastRadiusScore shape)
Question catalog present with [R/M/F] status markers and earns-pressure-for attribution
Design correctly identifies fingerprint #11 (External-Proxy Analysis Graph) — proves the skill can match by structure, not just by vocabulary

OVERFIT DETECTION: design's shape skeleton is structurally similar to prompt 1's (same number of relationship arities, same content-addressed-policy pattern, same anti-shapes discipline) but uses domain-specific names with no carry-over of `TicketProxy`, `TicketCluster`, etc.
Design does NOT use `originalWref: string` or any flat-string-wref-field pattern to encode a relationship endpoint
Design walks the convergence checkpoint explicitly (5 questions answered)
Universal foundations addressed: hierarchical names, descriptions, append-only revision, mirrored convenience fields where Pair/Set targets are used, D9 stack position answered

evals.prompt:
We collect customer feedback through five channels: support emails, in-app feedback widget submissions, support tickets in Zendesk, recorded sales-call transcripts, and Twitter mentions of our handle. We want to find when the same complaint shows up across multiple channels (often paraphrased differently), tag complaints by feature area (auth, mobile, billing, etc.), identify which complaints have been addressed by recent feature releases, and rank our investment priorities by how many complaints each potential investment would resolve. Some complaints are blockers for others (e.g. 'I can't reset my password' blocks 'I can't access my account on mobile').

Design the WarmHub graph for this.
evals.expected_output: A WarmHub graph design that recognizes this is a layered co-fingerprint: pattern-mining (#5) for theme discovery + external-proxy analysis (#11) for cross-channel relationship assertions. Should include FeedbackProxy (one Thing per channel, all subtypes of an external-proxy concept), ThemeHypothesis as graph-synthesized (D2=both), ClusterAssignment as Pair-targeted between FeedbackProxy and ThemeHypothesis, content-addressed clustering policy, BlockerAssertion as Pair-targeted between complaints, InvestmentRecommendation as graph-synthesized recommendation, and an interface-shape discussion explaining how the per-channel feedback layer interfaces with the theme-synthesis layer.
evals.purpose: Layered co-fingerprint test. The prompt naturally forces a hybrid of pattern-mining (#5) + external-proxy analysis (#11). Tests whether the layered-co-fingerprints section in the catalog actually fires when the prompt warrants it, or whether the skill collapses to a single-fingerprint design and ignores the second layer.

assertions.text: Design recognizes the layered co-fingerprint structure — explicitly identifies pattern-mining (#5) AND external-proxy analysis (#11) as both relevant
Design articulates the interface shape(s) bridging the per-channel proxy layer and the theme-synthesis layer (per the layered-co-fingerprints pattern in catalog)
Channel-specific feedback (FeedbackProxy or per-channel subtypes) modeled as external proxies — Things, not assertions
Theme synthesis uses content-addressed AnalyticalPolicy / ClusteringPolicy shape (D3=expensive)
Cross-channel duplicate-complaint relationship uses `about: { set: [...] }` (symmetric)
Blocker relationship uses `about: { pair: [blocker, blocked] }` (directional)
Theme-membership uses `about: { pair: [FeedbackProxy, ThemeHypothesis] }` or analogous Pair (with mirrored convenience fields)
Investment-priority-ranking is treated as a derived query (aggregation over Theme + complaint counts), NOT as a durable InvestmentRanking/PriorityShape shape
Design does NOT collapse the layering by ignoring either pattern-mining or external-proxy aspects
Design walks convergence checkpoint

evals.prompt:
We want to capture which Slack messages in our team channels best answer common questions that come up repeatedly. Sometimes the same question gets re-asked weeks later by a new team member; sometimes the best answer is buried in a thread reply rather than being the first response. We want to track which message-threads contain answer-quality content, link related questions across channels, and surface the canonical 'this is the answer' message for each recurring question pattern.

Help us design the graph.
evals.expected_output: A WarmHub graph design that diagnoses the actual fingerprint (pattern-mining #5 + external-proxy analysis #11 + lightweight literature-review #1 for canonical-answer curation) despite the operational-sounding 'messages, threads, channels' vocabulary. Should NOT default to ops-state-tracking (#4) just because the surface terms suggest it. Should include MessageProxy / ThreadProxy as external-proxy Things, RecurringQuestionPattern as graph-synthesized, BestAnswerAssertion as Pair-targeted (canonical-answer-of), SameQuestionAssertion as Set-targeted (symmetric).
evals.purpose: Fingerprint-misdirection test. The vocabulary ('messages,' 'threads,' 'channels') triggers ops-state-tracking pattern recognition. The actual structure is pattern-mining + external-proxy + curation. Tests whether the dimensions diagnostic correctly classifies the domain rather than letting surface vocabulary dictate the fingerprint match.

assertions.text: Design correctly does NOT pattern-match to ops-state-tracking (#4) despite messaging-platform vocabulary
Design includes graph-synthesized concept (RecurringQuestionPattern, QuestionCluster, or similar) as a Thing — not just message proxies
Best-answer relationship uses `about: { pair: [Answer, Question] }` or analogous Pair (directional: answers-are-of)
Same-question relationship uses `about: { set: [...] }` (symmetric)
Design diagnoses fingerprint as a hybrid (pattern-mining + external-proxy + curation), not a single match
MessageProxy / ThreadProxy treated as external proxies (Things with stable Slack message id), not as assertions or as bytes the graph owns
Design includes content-addressed policy shape if pattern-recognition / question-clustering uses expensive derivation
Question catalog ties each shape to ≥1 question with [R/M/F] status
Anti-shapes section excludes 'recurring question' as a query unless it's specifically a derived-query candidate

evals.prompt:
We're building a research graph to track legal precedent across U.S. federal courts. Court opinions cite other opinions; some citations *affirm* the cited case's reasoning, some *distinguish* the cited case (limit it to its facts), and some *overturn* it. We want to find the most-cited cases (centrality), identify cases that overturn the most prior precedent (signs of doctrinal shift), find inconsistent precedent (cases on the same legal question with conflicting holdings), and trace how a doctrinal line evolves across decades.

Design the graph.
evals.expected_output: A WarmHub graph extending literature-review (#1) where the citation edge-kind (Affirms / Distinguishes / Overturns) is itself load-bearing — modeled either as distinct assertion shapes per kind (AffirmsAssertion, DistinguishesAssertion, OverturnsAssertion) or as a single CitationAssertion with a typed `kind` field with semantics affecting traversal. Centrality and 'most-overturning' are derived queries. Doctrinal-line evolution is a multi-hop traversal, not a synthesized aggregate. Inconsistent-precedent detection is a query over conflict between Affirms and Overturns chains.
evals.purpose: Edge-type-as-load-bearing variant test. Literature-review fingerprint exists in catalog but its example (ClaimBasis as a uniform Pair-edge) doesn't model edge-kind diversity. Tests whether the skill recognizes the variant and adapts the design rather than porting ClaimBasis verbatim. Also tests centrality-as-derived-query discipline.

assertions.text: Design extends literature-review fingerprint with typed-edge-kind discipline — either distinct assertion shapes per kind, or a single shape with a typed kind enum whose semantics are described
Citation relationships use Pair-targeted `about` regardless of kind (not flat string fields for cited-case)
Centrality (most-cited) is treated as a derived query over CitationAssertions, NOT as a precomputed `centralityScore: number` on the case Thing
Doctrinal-line evolution is described as a graph traversal (walk through citations across time), not as a synthesized DoctrinalLine Thing or assertion
Inconsistent-precedent detection is a derived query (find cases where Affirms-of-X and Overturns-of-X coexist), not a stored Inconsistency assertion
Design does NOT port the literature-review entry's ClaimBasis verbatim — adapts the pattern to the edge-type-bearing variant
Design walks 'where it fails when transplanted' notes for fingerprint #1 and explains adaptations
Court opinions / cases modeled as external-proxy Things (citing existing court records via stable identity)
Question catalog with [R/M/F], anti-shapes section, convergence checkpoint

auto_assertion_grading_hints.auto_pattern_about_set: Output contains the substring `about: { set:` or `about: {set:` (regex with optional whitespace).
auto_assertion_grading_hints.auto_pattern_about_pair: Output contains the substring `about: { pair:` or `about: {pair:`.
auto_assertion_grading_hints.auto_pattern_about_triple: Output contains the substring `about: { triple:` or `about: {triple:`.
auto_assertion_grading_hints.auto_pattern_question_catalog_status: Output contains `[R]`, `[M]`, or `[F]` status markers in a query catalog context.
auto_assertion_grading_hints.auto_pattern_earns_pressure: Output contains the phrase `Earns pressure for:` or `earns pressure for`.
auto_assertion_grading_hints.auto_pattern_no_flat_string_wref: Output does NOT contain a pattern like `<endpointName>Wref: string` (e.g. `originalWref: string`, `blockerWref: string`) used to encode a relationship endpoint as a flat field. Detection: regex match for `[A-Za-z]+Wref\s*:\s*string` followed by absence of a corresponding `about: \{ (pair|set|triple|list)` — failure if found WITH no Pair/Set/Triple/List target on the same shape.
auto_assertion_grading_hints.auto_pattern_anti_shapes_section: Output contains a section heading or list explicitly labeled 'anti-shapes', 'queries not shapes', 'derived queries', or equivalent.

configurations_to_run.name: with_skill
configurations_to_run.description: Subagent loads the design-warmhub-repo skill and produces a design for the prompt.

configurations_to_run.name: without_skill
configurations_to_run.description: Same prompt, no skill loaded. Tells us how much value the skill adds versus a base model that knows what knowledge graphs are.

iteration_metadata.iteration_1_skip_rationale: Prompts 3 (layered co-fingerprints) and 5 (edge-type variant) are higher-difficulty tests of secondary skill features. Run them in iteration-2 only if iteration-1's baseline (1, 2, 4) is clean. If iteration-1 reveals the skill is overfit on baseline cases, fix that before testing the harder cases.
iteration_metadata.key_decisive_test: Eval 2 (vulnerability-disclosure). Compare its output structure to eval 1's (ticket-corpus). If structurally identical with renamed shapes, principles transferred. If eval 2's design quality drops noticeably or produces shapes that look like the ticket-corpus design with s/TicketProxy/VulnReport/, the skill is template-matching and needs hardening (more diverse worked examples in primitives.md, abstracted anti-pattern in pitfalls.md, etc.).
